image.subject: A slight 16-year-old French girl with cloudy pale eyes from congenital cataracts, wavy dark brown hair pulled back with a ribbon, delicate cheekbones, wearing a faded blue cotton dress with a small leather satchel, fingertips tracing the air in front of her, kneeling at a wooden table in a dim room, her fingers carefully moving across an intricate miniature wooden scale model of Paris streets and buildings, her expression calm and focused

storyboard.claim: Marie-Laure builds a tactile model of a city she cannot see — touch as a mode of perception.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Marie-Laure's fingers on the miniature city model, feeling rooftops and alleyways.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opening beat — no previous.
storyboard.addedInformation: Establishes Marie-Laure's blindness and her father's model as her way of navigating.

image.subject: An 18-year-old German soldier with striking white-blond hair, pale skin, sharp intelligent blue eyes, lean wiry build, wearing a rumpled grey Wehrmacht field uniform with radio headphones around his neck, hunched over a bulky military radio transceiver in a dim concrete room, turning a dial with intense concentration, green cathode light reflecting off his face

storyboard.claim: Werner tracks people through the same invisible waves that connect Marie-Laure to the world.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Werner operating a military radio, headphones on, hunting a signal.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the second protagonist as a mirror of the first.
storyboard.addedInformation: Same technology, opposite moral purpose — the duality that drives the entire book.

image.subject: A cramped dusty attic in a tall narrow house, wooden rafters overhead, a glowing radio transmitter with coiled copper wires on a wooden desk, a small round window overlooking a walled coastal city with orange fire light reflecting off stone buildings in the distance, the room lit only by the warm amber glow of vacuum tubes

storyboard.claim: From the attic, she broadcasts — the vertical architecture of convergence begins at the top.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The Saint-Malo attic with its radio transmitter, the burning city visible through the window.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Zooms into the specific vertical geography — attic above, cellar below.
storyboard.addedInformation: The physical arrangement of the climax: broadcasting from above, listening from below.

image.subject: A dark stone cellar beneath a medieval coastal house, heavy wooden ceiling beams cracked and sagging, a faint amber glow from a single oil lamp on the floor, a bulky military radio transceiver sitting on a rough wooden crate with its dials faintly lit, rubble and dust on the flagstone floor, 1944 wartime atmosphere

storyboard.claim: Down in the cellar he is listening — two lives bent toward a single architectural intersection.
storyboard.concreteVisual: No image — the word CONVERGENCE carries this transition beat.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Completes the vertical pair: attic (broadcasting) vs. cellar (listening).
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the entire analysis as an anatomy of this convergence.

image.subject: A modern analyst in a dark blazer over an open-collar shirt, gesturing while explaining, standing beside a large desk covered with open books and scattered manuscript pages, a softly lit study with bookshelves in the background

storyboard.claim: Title card — introducing the deep dive into Doerr's novel.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Title text only — ANTHONY DOERR as the anchor.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Standard intro beat after the cold open hook.
storyboard.addedInformation: Signals the format: analytical deep dive, not plot summary.

image.subject: A modern analyst in a dark blazer over an open-collar shirt, gesturing while explaining, leaning forward with intensity, one hand raised palm-out as if pressing an urgent point, dramatic side-lighting

storyboard.claim: Doerr does not ease you in — the stakes hit immediately.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Emphasis word STAKES on screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Transition from intro to the opening scene analysis.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sets expectation: this book opens at maximum intensity.

image.subject: An aerial view of a medieval walled coastal citadel built on a rocky peninsula jutting into the grey Atlantic ocean, narrow cobblestone streets and stone buildings packed tightly within high granite ramparts, the Brittany coast of France in late summer, dramatic overcast sky, 1940s wartime atmosphere

storyboard.claim: August 1944 — the walled citadel of Saint-Malo, the inferno begins.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Aerial view of Saint-Malo's walled city on its coastal peninsula.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Drops us into the time and place after the premise was set.
storyboard.addedInformation: Establishes the physical geography: a walled medieval city about to be destroyed.

image.subject: Thousands of white paper leaflets scattered mid-air drifting down from a cloudy grey sky over a medieval walled coastal city with slate rooftops, some leaflets landing on cobblestone streets, late summer light filtering through clouds

storyboard.claim: American bombers with deceptively gentle names rain leaflets before the fire.
storyboard.concreteVisual: WWII bombers overhead, leaflets falling like paper snow.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Zooms in from the city to the sky above it.
storyboard.addedInformation: The ironic contrast: beautiful names for instruments of destruction.

image.subject: Thousands of white paper leaflets drifting down through grey smoke-filled sky above the medieval stone walls and slate rooftops of a burning walled coastal city, some leaflets caught mid-air fluttering, others settling on cobblestones below

storyboard.claim: Thousands of warning leaflets descend — terrifying paper snow before the bombs.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Emphasis on LEAFLETS and WARNING carries the beat.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the bombing sequence — leaflets first, then fire.
storyboard.addedInformation: The formal courtesy of warning before annihilation.

image.subject: A row of spent incendiary bomb casings lying on a scorched cobblestone street beside a blackened stone wall, scorch marks radiating outward from each canister, wisps of white smoke still curling upward, 1944 wartime aftermath

storyboard.claim: After the leaflets come incendiary rounds — thermite and white phosphorus designed to melt stone.
storyboard.concreteVisual: No image — war violence triggers Flux content filter; emphasis words carry it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Escalation: leaflets gave way to actual destruction.
storyboard.addedInformation: The chemistry of destruction — these are weapons designed to burn beyond extinguishing.

image.subject: A devastated medieval European city seen from a low angle, stone building facades reduced to hollow shells, rubble filling the narrow streets, a single church spire still standing cracked against a smoky grey sky, 1944 wartime destruction in Brittany France

storyboard.claim: 72,000 pounds of explosives systematically erasing centuries of history in hours.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The stat 72,000 POUNDS dominates the screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Quantifies the destruction described in the previous two beats.
storyboard.addedInformation: Scale: centuries of human construction deleted in a single afternoon.

image.subject: A wide view of a walled medieval coastal city at night engulfed in orange flames, towering columns of fire and thick black smoke rising above the granite ramparts, the dark Atlantic ocean reflecting the firelight, 1944 Brittany France

storyboard.claim: A firestorm creates its own weather — sucking oxygen, erasing centuries.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Emphasis on FIRESTORM carries the physics.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Extends the destruction from quantity (72,000 lbs) to physics (self-sustaining fire).
storyboard.addedInformation: Firestorms generate their own wind systems, a detail Doerr uses precisely.

image.subject: A tall narrow stone house standing alone amid rubble and smoke in a devastated walled city, the house cracked but still upright, light glowing faintly from an attic window at the top and from a cellar grate at the bottom, smoke drifting through the empty street, 1944 Saint-Malo

storyboard.claim: In the center of the oxygen vacuum: two focal points, two lives.
storyboard.concreteVisual: FOCAL POINTS on screen, pivoting from destruction to the characters inside it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Transitions from the bombing's physics to the human lives at its center.
storyboard.addedInformation: Reframes the firestorm as backdrop; the real subject is the two people inside it.

image.subject: A slight 16-year-old French girl with cloudy pale eyes from congenital cataracts, wavy dark brown hair pulled back with a ribbon, delicate cheekbones, wearing a faded blue cotton dress with a small leather satchel, fingertips tracing the air in front of her, standing in the narrow dark stairwell of a tall old stone house, one hand touching the rough wall for guidance, dust motes floating in a sliver of light from a high window

storyboard.claim: In a tall narrow house on the Rue Vauborel: Marie-Laure, 16, completely blind.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Marie-Laure navigating the narrow stairwell of the Saint-Malo house by touch.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: First focal point identified — Marie-Laure in the tall house.
storyboard.addedInformation: Grounds her physically in the specific building that becomes the climax's axis.

image.subject: Close-up of a small intricately carved wooden puzzle box with hidden sliding panels and brass inlays sitting on a rough wooden floor beside a narrow iron bed frame, a faint blue-white gleam visible through a tiny gap in the wood suggesting a gemstone hidden inside, dust and plaster debris scattered around, dim wartime room

storyboard.claim: She shelters under her bed clutching a puzzle box containing a mythical diamond.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The wooden puzzle box on the floor, hint of the diamond's gleam inside.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Zooms into what Marie-Laure holds — the object that drives the antagonist's hunt.
storyboard.addedInformation: The Sea of Flames diamond, cursed: the holder lives forever, but everyone they love dies.

image.subject: An 18-year-old German soldier with striking white-blond hair, pale skin, sharp intelligent blue eyes, lean wiry build, wearing a rumpled grey Wehrmacht field uniform with radio headphones around his neck, standing in a narrow cobblestone alley between medieval stone walls, military radio equipment strapped to his back, looking upward with a conflicted expression, wartime 1944

storyboard.claim: Blocks away: Werner Pfennig, 18, German radio operator with stark white hair.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Werner in the streets of Saint-Malo with his radio equipment.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Second focal point — the mirror image, just blocks from Marie-Laure.
storyboard.addedInformation: His distinctive white hair is a visual signature Doerr returns to constantly.

image.subject: A collapsed interior of a grand old stone hotel, heavy wooden beams and chunks of masonry piled in chaotic layers, dust thick in the air, a narrow gap between fallen stones where a faint light penetrates, a rumpled grey military uniform sleeve and white-blond hair barely visible beneath the debris, 1944 wartime destruction

storyboard.claim: Werner is trapped beneath the rubble of the Hotel of Bees.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The collapsed hotel interior, Werner buried under debris.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Specifies Werner's predicament — buried alive, still listening.
storyboard.addedInformation: The Hotel of Bees is where Werner's unit was stationed when the bombing hit.

image.subject: An 18-year-old German soldier with striking white-blond hair, pale skin, sharp intelligent blue eyes, lean wiry build, wearing a rumpled grey Wehrmacht field uniform with radio headphones around his neck, adjusting a large directional radio antenna mounted on a tripod in a dim concrete room, a paper map pinned to the wall behind him with pencil lines converging on a single point

storyboard.claim: Werner's mission: use a directional transceiver to triangulate her position and eliminate her.
storyboard.concreteVisual: TRIANGULATE and ELIMINATE on screen — the mission stated in stark terms.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Reveals the lethal purpose connecting the two focal points.
storyboard.addedInformation: Their lives were engineered to collide: hunter and hunted on the same frequency.

image.subject: A thick hardcover novel lying open face-down on a worn wooden desk, its pages fanned out showing hundreds of densely printed pages, a pair of reading glasses resting beside it, warm lamplight casting long shadows across the desk surface

storyboard.claim: Doerr spends 500 pages proving this intersection was never accidental.
storyboard.concreteVisual: 500 PAGES as emphasis — the scale of Doerr's argument.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Pulls back from the scene to the author's structural intent.
storyboard.addedInformation: The entire novel is an elaborate proof of inevitability.

image.subject: A modern analyst in a dark blazer over an open-collar shirt, gesturing while explaining, standing at a lectern with one hand placed flat on an open book, looking directly forward with conviction, warm studio lighting

storyboard.claim: This brings us to the actual thesis Doerr is presenting.
storyboard.concreteVisual: THESIS on screen, signaling the analytical pivot.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Transition from the scene description to the book's deeper argument.
storyboard.addedInformation: Signals that what follows is the intellectual core, not just plot.

image.subject: A long column of civilian refugees walking along a dusty French country road in summer 1940, carrying suitcases and bundles, horse-drawn carts loaded with belongings, children clutching parents hands, green hedgerows on both sides, overcast sky, wartime exodus

storyboard.claim: It is easy to categorize this as a beautifully written WWII survival epic — but that misses the point.
storyboard.concreteVisual: WORLD WAR II and SURVIVAL EPIC on screen as the surface label.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sets up the contrast: what most readers see vs. what Doerr built.
storyboard.addedInformation: The beautiful prose is a delivery mechanism, not the payload.

image.subject: Close-up of an open hardcover book with elegant printed text on cream-colored pages, soft golden light falling across the page from a nearby window, a fountain pen resting in the gutter between the pages

storyboard.claim: The prose is gorgeous — but that is a surface-level appreciation.
storyboard.concreteVisual: GORGEOUS PROSE as emphasis, brief acknowledgement before the pivot.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Concedes the beauty before arguing it distracts from the architecture.
storyboard.addedInformation: Brief beat — validates the common reader response to pivot past it.

image.subject: An architectural blueprint spread across a drafting table, precise ink lines showing the cross-section of a tall narrow multi-story house with an attic at the top and a cellar at the bottom, compass and drafting tools beside the paper, warm desk lamp light

storyboard.claim: The underlying architecture of this narrative is something far more ambitious.
storyboard.concreteVisual: ARCHITECTURE on screen — the structural claim.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Pivots from surface beauty to the hidden structural argument.
storyboard.addedInformation: Doerr is not just telling a story; he is building an argument.

image.subject: A modern analyst in a dark blazer over an open-collar shirt, gesturing while explaining, one finger raised to emphasize a point, standing in front of a dark chalkboard with faintly visible chalk diagrams of branching paths and question marks

storyboard.claim: The narrative is an intricate argument about epistemology — how we know what we know.
storyboard.concreteVisual: EPISTEMOLOGY dominates the screen as the core concept.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the intellectual framework the entire analysis will use.
storyboard.addedInformation: Epistemology: the study of how knowledge is acquired, validated, and transmitted.

image.subject: A large military radio transmitter with glowing vacuum tubes and coiled copper antenna wires sitting on a steel desk in a 1940s military signals room, a pair of headphones resting on the desk, green indicator lights glowing, the room otherwise dark and utilitarian

storyboard.claim: The most dangerous weapon in any war is not a bomb — it is the transmission of knowledge.
storyboard.concreteVisual: TRANSMISSION and KNOWLEDGE as emphasis — the thesis stated plainly.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Applies the epistemology framework to the war setting.
storyboard.addedInformation: Doerr argues that data, not ordnance, determines who wins and who dies.

image.subject: A cluttered wooden shelf holding a collection of 1940s communication objects: a handheld crystal radio receiver, a cylindrical wax phonograph record, a small round loaf of bread with a slip of paper tucked inside, and a worn leather-bound storybook, all lit by warm lamplight against a dark background

storyboard.claim: A radio signal, a bedtime story, a wax cylinder recording, a coded number in a loaf of bread.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Four forms of knowledge transmission listed on screen.
storyboard.onScreenText: RADIO SIGNAL / BEDTIME STORY / WAX CYLINDER / CODED NUMBERS
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Enumerates the specific transmission forms Doerr uses in the novel.
storyboard.addedInformation: Each item in the list appears in the book as a weapon or a lifeline.

image.subject: Two identical vintage radio receivers side by side on a wooden table, the left one draped with a dark military field map and a pair of Wehrmacht headphones, the right one with a small French tricolor ribbon and a worn copy of Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea beside it, dramatic split lighting warm on the right and cold on the left

left.label: WEAPON
left.subject: Information used for mass destruction — Werner's radio triangulation, Nazi propaganda broadcasts, coded military orders

right.label: LIBERATION
right.subject: Information used for total liberation — Etienne's Resistance broadcasts, Marie-Laure reading Verne into the transmitter, coded bread messages

storyboard.claim: A piece of information can be a weapon of mass destruction or a tool of total liberation.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Split screen: WEAPON vs. LIBERATION — same data, opposite moral charge.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Resolves the list into its binary: every form of data serves one of two masters.
storyboard.addedInformation: The identical radio wave can track a target or broadcast hope.

image.subject: Close-up of a hand turning the brass tuning dial of a vintage 1940s radio receiver, the dial marked with frequency numbers, warm amber light from the glowing vacuum tubes reflecting off the metal faceplate, shallow depth of field

storyboard.claim: It depends entirely on who controls the frequency.
storyboard.concreteVisual: CONTROLS THE FREQUENCY on screen — the power question.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the weapon-vs-liberation split: the controller decides.
storyboard.addedInformation: Doerr then pushes further into a moral claim about sight itself.

image.subject: A slight 16-year-old French girl with cloudy pale eyes from congenital cataracts, wavy dark brown hair pulled back with a ribbon, delicate cheekbones, wearing a faded blue cotton dress with a small leather satchel, fingertips tracing the air in front of her, standing in bright sunlight on a cobblestone street with her face turned upward and a serene expression, light falling full on her face while shadowy figures in Wehrmacht uniforms pass blurred in the dark background behind her

storyboard.claim: Blindness and sight are not biological conditions of the optic nerve.
storyboard.concreteVisual: SIGHT and BLINDNESS as emphasis — redefining both terms.
storyboard.onScreenText: SIGHT AND BLINDNESS ARE NOT PHYSICAL CONDITIONS
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Elevates from epistemology to Doerr's moral redefinition.
storyboard.addedInformation: This reframes the entire novel: Marie-Laure sees more than the sighted characters.

image.subject: A faceless modern figure in a plain dark hoodie, illuminated by the blue glow of a screen, headphones on, turning away from the screen with one hand covering their eyes, the screen casting sharp blue light into a dark room

storyboard.claim: Sight and blindness are moral choices — the worst acts come from those with functioning eyes who choose not to see.
storyboard.concreteVisual: MORAL CHOICES dominates the screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Completes the redefinition: blindness is chosen, not inherited.
storyboard.addedInformation: The true blind are those who look away — Werner during Frederick's beating, the complicit bystanders.

image.subject: A faceless modern figure in a plain dark hoodie, illuminated by the blue glow of a screen, headphones on, slumped in a chair scrolling a phone, dozens of faint ghostly news headlines and images floating past in the air around them unnoticed, a dark room lit only by the device glow

storyboard.claim: The true casualties are people with perfect eyes who consciously tune out suffering.
storyboard.concreteVisual: TUNE OUT and SUFFERING — a direct challenge to the viewer.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the moral claim from historical to personal — addressing the viewer.
storyboard.addedInformation: Bridges WWII complicity to modern passive consumption.

image.subject: A faceless modern figure in a plain dark hoodie, illuminated by the blue glow of a screen, headphones on, surrounded by invisible radio waves rendered as faint concentric circles of light emanating from all directions, sitting alone in a dark room, the waves passing through the figure's body unseen

storyboard.claim: Invisible waves are passing through your physical space right now — think about them.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The Everyman surrounded by invisible signals in a modern dark room.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Makes the book's 1944 theme viscerally present for the modern viewer.
storyboard.addedInformation: The same physics that carried Nazi orders and Resistance broadcasts now carries Wi-Fi and algorithms.

image.subject: A wooden desk with a vintage radio receiver on the left and a modern smartphone on the right, both glowing softly, warm amber light from the radio and cool blue light from the phone meeting in the middle of the desk

storyboard.claim: Wi-Fi, cellular signals, targeted algorithmic feeds — are you choosing which to decode?
storyboard.concreteVisual: Three modern signal types listed on screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Specifies the modern equivalent of WWII radio frequencies.
storyboard.addedInformation: Updates Doerr's metaphor: the frequency question is now about social media and algorithms.

image.subject: A faceless modern figure in a plain dark hoodie sitting in a dark room, one hand deliberately turning a dial on a vintage radio receiver, the other hand pushing away a wall of flickering screens and blurry social media feeds crowding in from the opposite side

storyboard.claim: Are you actively choosing your frequencies, or passively letting noise wash over you?
storyboard.concreteVisual: CHOOSING vs. PASSIVE — the central question posed directly.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Distills the entire thesis into a single binary question for the viewer.
storyboard.addedInformation: The difference between these two states is literally everything, per Doerr.

image.subject: A slight 16-year-old French girl with cloudy pale eyes from congenital cataracts, wavy dark brown hair pulled back with a ribbon, delicate cheekbones, wearing a faded blue cotton dress with a small leather satchel, fingertips tracing the air in front of her, seated at a wooden desk in a sunlit room running her fingertips carefully over the surface of a large seashell, her face tilted in concentration, stacks of specimen boxes and Braille books around her

storyboard.claim: To learn active perception, look at Marie-Laure's education.
storyboard.concreteVisual: MARIE-LAURE and EDUCATION on screen, pivoting to the next section.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Transitions from the modern challenge back to the novel's demonstration of it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Marie-Laure's training by her father is Doerr's model for how active perception works.

image.subject: A slight 16-year-old French girl with cloudy pale eyes from congenital cataracts, wavy dark brown hair pulled back with a ribbon, delicate cheekbones, wearing a faded blue cotton dress with a small leather satchel, fingertips tracing the air in front of her, standing in the grand gallery of a natural history museum with tall glass specimen cases of minerals and shells around her, her hands reaching out to touch the edge of a wooden display cabinet, soft amber light filtering through high windows

storyboard.claim: A child who lost her sight to congenital cataracts at age six learns to map reality without vision.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Marie-Laure navigating the museum by touch, surrounded by specimens she cannot see.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Begins the education arc — how blindness became her mode of deeper perception.
storyboard.addedInformation: Congenital cataracts: she had some vision as a very young child, then lost it entirely.

image.subject: A stocky 45-year-old French craftsman with calloused steady hands, a kind square face, short dark hair greying at the temples, wearing a brown wool museum worker's coat with tiny brass keys on a ring at his belt, kneeling beside a slight young French girl with cloudy pale eyes and wavy dark brown hair, guiding her small hands across an intricate miniature wooden scale model of Paris streets on a workbench, warm workshop light, tools and wood shavings on the table

storyboard.claim: Her father Daniel teaches her to map reality without vision — through the miniature city model.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Daniel guiding Marie-Laure's hands across the wooden model of Paris.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces Daniel as the architect of Marie-Laure's perception training.
storyboard.addedInformation: He builds the model so she can memorize every street by touch before walking it.

image.subject: A stocky 45-year-old French craftsman with calloused steady hands, a kind square face, short dark hair greying at the temples, wearing a brown wool museum worker's coat with tiny brass keys on a ring at his belt, placing a finished miniature wooden building onto an intricate scale model of a city laid out on a workbench, his expression warm and determined, workshop tools hanging on the wall behind him

storyboard.claim: Daniel fundamentally rejects the idea that blindness is a barrier to understanding the world.
storyboard.concreteVisual: NOT A BARRIER as emphasis — Daniel's core philosophy.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: States Daniel's philosophy that drives everything he builds for Marie-Laure.
storyboard.addedInformation: This mirrors Doerr's thesis: real blindness is moral, not optical.

image.subject: A stocky 45-year-old French craftsman with calloused steady hands, a kind square face, short dark hair greying at the temples, wearing a brown wool museum worker's coat with tiny brass keys on a ring at his belt, working at a wooden bench in the back rooms of a grand natural history museum, surrounded by brass lock mechanisms and tiny precision tools, examining an ornate antique lock under a magnifying lamp, glass specimen cases visible through an open doorway behind him

storyboard.claim: Daniel is the principal locksmith at the Muséum National d'Histoire Naturelle in Paris.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Daniel at his workbench in the museum, surrounded by locks and tools.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Grounds Daniel's philosophy in his profession — a man who opens sealed things.
storyboard.addedInformation: His job is literally to control access to knowledge — keys, tumblers, mechanisms.

image.subject: Close-up of an ornate brass lock mechanism disassembled on a wooden workbench, its tiny tumblers and springs laid out in precise order, a magnifying loupe and fine watchmaker's tools beside the parts, warm lamplight gleaming on the polished brass components

storyboard.claim: Daniel's existence revolves around mechanisms, tumblers, and the philosophy of access.
storyboard.concreteVisual: TUMBLERS and PHILOSOPHY on screen — the locksmith as philosopher.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Extends from his job to his worldview: every lock is a puzzle about who gets to know.
storyboard.addedInformation: A lock restricts knowledge or value — Daniel's craft is the book's epistemology in miniature.
